newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes shade up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes shade up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade up on Thursday from New York's previous close after a bout of shortcovering when Europe opened, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$339.50/340.00 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$339.30/80 close on Wednesday.
"After Europe opened we saw some shortcovering," said one dealer.
Others also reported shortcovering from the local market.
Sentiment remained bearish and dealers said the market would test lower.
Traders pegged near-term support at between $336 and $337.50, while resistence was seen at $341 to $343.
Physical demand was weak, traders said.
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,147 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from its previous fix at -3.05.
